samples.summary: Large unrequested scope beyond the issue's single acceptance criterion
samples.evidence: The issue's acceptance criterion is one line: "Type text, select it, reset the text color → the text is uncolored (default ink), not the selection color." The branch satisfies that with the toolbar `undefined` change plus `resolveStoredColor` in the paint paths. Everything else is additional programs of work: OOXML injection hardening of non-color attributes (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/{shape,connector,layout,animation,theme}.ts`, docs `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS`/`toHeadingStyleId`), a new ~350-line backend PUT validation contract for docs *and* slides bodies (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts`), a shared CRDT attribute codec (`packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts`), and two independent Yorkie CRDT bugs (`removeNodeStyle` subtree over-removal, the `setBlockType` table-inline splice). The branch's own todo file ("Scope grown during review", lines 116-166) acknowledges this and argues against splitting. Each of items 3, 4 and 6 there is independently issue-worthy, testable and revertible, and none is needed for the stated outcome — this is the definition of scope creep for this lane, even if each item is defensible on its merits.

samples.summary: Inline-run validation duplicated between the docs arm and the slides arm of the same file
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` gains an inline loop (not-an-object / `text` must be string / `style` must be object) and `normalizeSlideInlines` re-implements the same three checks with the same message strings a few hundred lines below. The only difference is the repair of an absent `inlines`/`style`. One helper parameterized by "repair vs reject" would express the difference; as written the two copies will drift, which is exactly the failure mode the change's own `crdt-attrs.ts` extraction exists to prevent.

samples.summary: Only block style was deduplicated; inline-style and cell-style codecs stay duplicated, and the new design doc overclaims
samples.evidence: The new docs-collaboration.md section states the Tree attribute codec "is a single shared module ... Both sides import it; neither keeps a copy, because a divergence would make one writer's output unreadable by the other's reader." That reasoning applies verbatim to `serializeInlineStyle`/`parseInlineStyle`/`serializeCellStyle`, which still exist as independent copies in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:110,169,228` and `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:68,100,148`. The extraction is half-done and the doc reads as if it were complete.

samples.summary: Validator silently mutates (repairs) the request body inside `assertValid*` functions, and the two arms of the endpoint follow opposite policies
samples.evidence: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` assigns `body.blocks = []`, `assertValidSlideBlocks` assigns `block.style = {}`, and `normalizeSlideInlines` assigns `block.inlines = []` / `inline.style = {}`. Functions named `assert…` that mutate their input are a surprising abstraction; a separate `normalizeSlidesBody()` pass before `assertValidSlidesBody()` would express "repair then validate" honestly. Compounding it, the docs arm 400s on exactly the shapes the slides arm silently repairs (absent `style`, absent `inlines`), so one endpoint now has two contradictory policies for the same `Block` shape. rest-api.md documents the asymmetry, so it is a deliberate design choice — but it is the kind of split contract that invites future divergence.

samples.summary: The user-visible contract change (color reset clears the key; `''` means unset) is not recorded in the docs design docs that own the text-color control
samples.evidence: docs-font-controls.md is the canonical doc for the TextColor/Highlight toolbar controls and `InlineStyle.color`/`backgroundColor` (lines 262-263, 301, 320) but is untouched. The new "empty string is a legacy value meaning unset, normalized on both sides of the ColorResolver via `resolveStoredColor`" convention — the actual fix for the issue — is only described in the two *export* design docs and in code comments. A reader of the docs area's design docs cannot learn the render-side convention.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out in the tree. The todo file's "Scope grown during review" section (lines 116-166) exists verbatim and itself states items 2-6 are "not" issue #728, against a single acceptance criterion at lines 168-171. Each cited program of work is really present: closed-Map OOXML hardening for non-color attributes in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts (PRST_BY_KIND at :24, DASH_VAL at :132) and sibling connector/layout/animation/theme files; a large PUT validation contract in packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts (assertValidDocsBody :245, assertValidSlidesBody :452, assertValidBlockStyle :330, assertValidTextBodyBlocks :654); the shared codec packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:1-40; and the CRDT style-removal rework in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts (removedCellStyleAttrs :250, removeNodeStyle :273, call sites :1459, :2459, :2470, :2520). No guard or caller makes this unreachable, and unrequested scope creep is explicitly inside this lens's lane, so neither not-present, already-guarded, nor out-of-scope applies. The branch's own claim that design-fit previously rated the scope non-blocking is branch-authored text, not a repo rule, and cannot ground a refutation.

finding.summary: Large unrequested scope beyond issue #728: OOXML hardening of non-color attributes across four exporters (shape `prst` allowlist, animation int coercion, connector/layout/theme Maps, DOCX `w:jc`/`w:pStyle`) is neither in the issue's acceptance criterion nor in the task plan.
finding.evidence: The originating issue (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:102-105) has exactly one acceptance criterion: "Type text, select it, reset the text color → the text is uncolored (default ink), not the selection color." Its Plan (lines 21-101) covers the toolbar reset, the renderer `resolveStoredColor` guard, and the *color* normalizer at the DOCX/PPTX color sinks. The diff additionally rewrites `PRST_BY_KIND` (~90 shape kinds), `DASH_VAL`, `TYPE_TO_TAG`/`DIR_TO_ATTR`/`EFFECT_TO_PRESET`/`START_TO_NODE_TYPE`/`toXmlInt` in animation.ts, `ROUTING_PRST`/`KIND_TO_OOXML`/`SIZE_TO_OOXML` in connector.ts, `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE` in layout.ts, `ALGN`/`UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U`/`listLevelAttr` in text.ts, and `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS`/`toHeadingStyleId` in docx-style-map.ts — none of which touch color. Each is defensible on its own but belongs to a separate 'OOXML attribute sinks are closed' change with its own issue/plan, and bundling them makes the color-reset fix hard to review or revert independently.

verdict.reason: The flagged code exists (shape.ts:24/97/132/153, animation.ts:60/82/152/218-258), so this is not a phantom, but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) The finding's core premise is factually wrong: the work IS in the task plan — docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:136-143 enumerates exactly "Shape prst, prstDash, algn, arrowheads, connector routing, layout type, transition tag, animation integers, DOCX w:jc / w:pStyle / heading ids … converted to closed Map lookups and numeric coercion", with the split decision recorded at :159-166. (b) No stated Non-Goal is exceeded: todo.md:205-213, slides-pptx-export.md:55-70, docs-docx-import-export.md:31-37 cover palette/picker/migration, pixel parity/charts/PDF/image-upload, and round-trip fidelity/floating images — none of them this. The pptx Goal at :38-39 ("serialize to a valid .pptx") is what the closed-Map work serves. (c) Design-doc discipline is met inside the canonical subsystem doc, not a parallel file: slides-pptx-export.md:213-226 documents the animation closed Maps and integer coercion, :148-172 and :201-208 the color/theme sinks. (d) The originating acceptance criterion is implemented (text-format-group.tsx:124-128,252,347 reset with undefined; resolveStoredColor in packages/docs/src/model/color.ts, view/paint-layout.ts, view/table-renderer.ts). What remains is the reviewer's own stated concern — bundling makes the fix "hard to review or revert independently" — a PR-hygiene preference, which the rubric classifies as minor/nit and never blocking, especially with the scope chain documented in-repo.
